summary: Phase 4 leaderboard schema, ranking route, and dialog difficulty keys are correctly implemented. The shared leaderboardResponseSchema has an honest schoolScoped: true marker, canonical difficulty keys (easy/medium/hard/extreme, no normal), and rankingRoute.ts validates against the schema. RankingDialog.tsx uses medium as the default tab. Non-blocking contract gap documented: dialog expects difficulty-keyed object but route returns flat array; must be resolved in Phase 5+.
nonblocking_findings: NB-P4-001: RankingDialog.tsx expects a difficulty-keyed Record (data?.[diff]) but rankingRoute.ts returns a flat array per leaderboardResponseSchema. With empty mock data this is invisible; must be resolved in Phase 5+ when real data flows.
NB-P4-002: DIFFICULTY_KEYS is exported from rankingRoute.ts but RankingDialog.tsx hardcodes its own difficulties array. Phase 5+ should import DIFFICULTY_KEYS to stay in sync.
NB-P4-003: 65 legacy 'normal' difficulty references remain across other games; Phase 5+ scope per Decision 4.3.
evidence: packages/domain/src/games/schema.ts defines leaderboardEntrySchema + leaderboardResponseSchema with schoolScoped: z.literal(true).
rankingRoute.ts validates response via leaderboardResponseSchema.parse() and uses DIFFICULTY_KEYS = ['easy','medium','hard','extreme'].
RankingDialog.tsx uses TabDifficulty type with medium and defaultValue='medium'.
rankingRoute.test.ts 7/7 pass including 'does not include legacy normal difficulty key' (B21-018).
live_contract_violations: LCV-P4-001: RankingDialog flat-array vs keyed-object mismatch — route returns flat array per leaderboardResponseSchema, dialog expects difficulty-keyed Record. Non-blocking for Phase 4 (empty mock), blocking for Phase 5+.
